category_title: Students who commit property damage but demonstrate accountability
student_description: Felix is a student who occasionally damages property during physical horseplay but demonstrates strong accountability by immediately attempting to fix his mistakes. He has external rehabilitation commitments (drug and alcohol classes) and vocational strengths (construction). The evidence reveals he uniquely needs flexible, restorative consequences that accommodate his schedule and empower him to use his hands-on skills to make amends.

criteria.rationale: Felix attends after-school drug and alcohol classes, so imposing standard after-school consequences creates unmanageable conflicts and ignores his rehabilitation efforts.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must acknowledge or accommodate Felix's existing after-school schedule rather than assigning conflicting mandatory after-school time.

criteria.rationale: Felix demonstrates accountability and possesses construction skills, making hands-on repair a more effective and respectful consequence than standard punitive measures.
criteria.check: The tutor's response must allow, encourage, or explore the option for Felix to use his specific vocational skills (e.g., construction) to repair the damage he caused.
